title: Comfort & Sleep Routines
strapline: The same gentle wind-down, the same familiar arms, the same quiet song — a baby who feels safe enough to let go and sleep.
intent: Give every baby a predictable, comforting wind-down to sleep, honouring their own rhythm rather than a fixed clock.
Deepen the bond and trust that let a baby settle — sleep comes most easily to a baby who feels safe and held.
Support co-regulation, as a calm key person helps a tired or unsettled baby move down into rest.
Help babies anticipate and feel secure in the familiar sequence — cuddle, comforter, song, sleep — knowing what comes next.
Work closely with families so sleep at nursery echoes the comfort of sleep at home.
implementation: Follow each baby's own sleep cues and rhythm — drooping eyes, grizzling, a comforter reached for — rather than a whole-room nap time.
Keep a consistent wind-down: dimmed light, quieter voices, the same lullaby, the baby's own comforter and sleep space.
Let the key person, wherever possible, be the one who settles their key babies, holding, patting or simply being close.
Gather each family's sleep routine and words — how they soothe, what they sing, the comforter's name — and mirror it faithfully.
Follow safer-sleep practice throughout, check sleeping babies as your policy requires, and keep the space calm, warm and dim.
key_questions: Are your eyes telling me you're getting sleepy?
Shall we get your comforter and sing our sleep song?
Would a cuddle help you settle?
Is this how Mummy helps you go to sleep at home?
You had such a good rest — are you ready to wake up gently?

impact.text: Babies settle to sleep and wake into predictable, responsive rhythms, their own cues followed and honoured.
A tired or unsettled baby is soothed by their familiar key person and comforter, calming through gentle co-regulation.
The warm, consistent wind-down deepens the baby's bond with their key person, comforted and safe enough to sleep.
Babies come to anticipate the familiar sequence — cuddle, comforter, song, sleep — secure in knowing what comes next.

enhancements: A recorded family lullaby or the key person's own quiet song for the wind-down.
Each baby's own comforter and sleep sack, kept consistent between home and nursery.
A calm, dimmable sleep space away from the busy room.
A shared home-nursery sleep log so routines and cues stay in step with families.
A gentle waking routine — soft light, a familiar face, no rush — so babies surface calmly.

playing_exploring: The baby's own cues and comforts lead the way down into rest, at their own pace.
Familiar sounds, scents and holding make settling feel safe.
active_learning: A baby learns, over settled days, that rest here is safe, and lets go into sleep more easily.
creating_thinking: A baby begins to recognise the wind-down sequence and anticipate the sleep it leads to.
